description.html: This decoration shows a shipwreck the sea has completely taken over: the hull is broken and overgrown with moss and roots, and the gray-green tones make it look like something that has lain on the bottom for decades. There is an opening in the hull for fish to swim in and out, and the broken parts create additional cover.

Thanks to its low, elongated shape, the wreck fits nicely in the front or middle of the aquarium and does not block the view of the rest of the setup. The muted colors go easily with live plants, stones and roots, so it suits more natural aquariums, not just themed ones.

Before use, rinse the wreck in lukewarm water, without detergents. Set it on a flat surface and press it lightly into the sand or gravel so it does not shift. If you keep fish that dig in the bottom, check after a few days that it is still stable. Clean algae and debris from the crevices with a soft brush during regular water changes.
